description: What each SCALAR operator of esm-spec §9.2's evaluable core COMPUTES, pinned once for every binding. The op vocabulary is named in the spec and its tiers are gated by the registry corpus, but nothing shared said what `sign(0)`, `7/2`, `atan2(y, x)` or a false comparison is WORTH — each binding pinned it privately, against its own evaluator, in its own vocabulary: Julia through `build_evaluator` on hand-built AST nodes (tree_walk_test.jl), Rust through `interpret()` on a `ResolvedExpr` tree (interpret.rs), Python through `_expr_to_sympy` unit tests (test_simulation_scalar_ops.py). Three private op tables and no cross-binding gate is exactly the shape in which two bindings disagree for a year. The fixture is ALGEBRAIC: every operator is an observed whose operands are declared PARAMETERS, asserted at a single static evaluation (CONFORMANCE_SPEC §5.43), so no integrator stands between the operator and the number and the band is the arithmetic's alone. A second test re-asserts a subset under `parameter_overrides`, so a binding that folded the declared defaults at build time and ignored the overrides lands on the first test's numbers and fails.

scope_excluded.go: No simulator and no inline-test runner, so a tier that DRIVES one cannot be run here (API_SPEC.md §3, capability profiles). This is an exclusion from the CATEGORY, not from the rule.
scope_excluded.typescript: No simulator and no inline-test runner, so a tier that DRIVES one cannot be run here (API_SPEC.md §3, capability profiles). This is an exclusion from the CATEGORY, not from the rule.

tolerances.detail: §5.38.2's `algebraic` class. These are single evaluations of scalar arithmetic, so two correct bindings differ only in the last bits of a transcendental; nothing here carries an integrator's error except the one `probe` assertion, which declares its own looser band in the document.
